narrative.summary: Botswana has no published AI law or AI strategy. Its binding AI-relevant rules are in the Data Protection Act 2024, in force since January 2025, which restricts decisions based solely on automated processing and profiling and requires impact assessments for automated evaluation. A National AI Policy is reported as being finalised by the Ministry of Communications and Innovation, and no official public copy of the 2020 SmartBots digital transformation strategy has been identified.
narrative.review_notes: Not yet verified from the official text: the National AI Policy (reported as being finalised) and the 2020 SmartBots digital transformation strategy. Official sources checked on 12 and 18 October 2026 include the national law portal, Parliament, the communications regulator, the central bank and government news, with no further AI-specific document identified; still to check: the government portal and ministry pages, the data protection commission, the digital innovation hub, the procurement authority and the standards bureau.

instruments.current_status: Enacted by the Parliament of Botswana; date of assent 24 October 2024 (the Act states no separate gazette publication date, so the assent date is used). In operation from 14 January 2025 under the Data Protection Act (Date of Commencement) Order, 2025 (S.I. No. 4 of 2025, made and published 13 January 2025). It repeals and replaces the Data Protection Act, 2018 (Act No. 32 of 2018, Cap. 43:14; commenced by S.I. 86 of 2021, amended by Act 33 of 2022) and continues the Information and Data Protection Commission. No AI-specific guidance from the Commission was found.
instruments.summary: Botswana's general data protection law, which continues the Information and Data Protection Commission and regulates the processing of personal data by public and private controllers and processors, including foreign controllers targeting data subjects in Botswana. Section 49 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal effects or similarly significant effects, with exceptions for contracts, explicit consent or authorisation by law, and requires safeguards including human intervention, the right to express a view and to contest the decision. Section 65 requires a data protection impact assessment before high-risk processing using new technologies, expressly including systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects based on automated processing and profiling.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding rules on solely automated decision-making and profiling (s.49) and mandatory impact assessments for automated evaluation (s.65); the main binding legal constraint on AI systems processing personal data in Botswana.

leads.title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy (Botswana)
leads.note: Government news (Daily News, 13 August 2025) reports the Assistant Minister of Communications and Innovation saying the Government is finalising a National AI Policy, following a UNESCO AI Readiness Assessment (RAM) validated in May 2025; an earlier 2024 report mentioned an AI strategy being developed with Estonia. No draft or adopted text was found on an official site on 2026-10-12 (gov.bw had an expired TLS certificate and returned 503). Record as national_strategy (or consultation_draft) once published. 2026-10-18: re-checked; the official Daily News articles of 12 and 13 August 2025 were opened and still describe the policy as being finalised. No draft or adopted text found on any reachable official site; the government portal and ministry pages still could not be opened. Kept as a lead.
